newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ consumer confidence extends downtrend - survey.
newsitem.headline: NZ consumer confidence extends downtrend - survey.

text.p: New Zealand consumer confidence fell sharply in the March 1997 quarter, according to a survey of consumer confidence published on Friday.
The WestpacTrust McDermott Miller Survey said its consumer confidence index eased to 115.6 in March, down 5.6 index points from 121.2 in December 1996, and down 13.2 points from 128.8 a year ago.

"This result continues the gradual downward trend observed in the index since the peak in June 1994 and is consistent with the slowdown in retail sales and general economic growth observed over that period," WestpacTrust's chief economist

"The overall level of confidence remains consistent with the soft landing scenario. The index remains in excess of 100 which indicates more optimists than pessimists. This suggests a period of slower growth rather than a sharp contraction in retail sales."
Graham said the fall in confidence in the March quarter had largely been driven by lower confidence about the outlook for the economy in general.
"Optimism regarding the one year outlook for the economy has been quite volatile over recent quarters, which is to be expected as the economy reaches a turning point."
Graham said confidence levels for the five year outlook for the economy recorded its lowest level since the December quarter of 1991.

"This possibly reflects some residual political uncertainty with respondents still unsure about what the new government means for them. This is the first survey to fully capture the reaction to the formation of the coalition government in December last year."
The conservative National Party and the nationalist New Zealand First Party formed a coalition government on December 10, 1996, following an inconclusive general election on October 12.

WestpacTrust said respondents were not as optimistic in the March quarter regarding their current or future financial situation. This reflected lower expectations of interest rate falls, and followed recent moves by most lenders to increase fixed rate home loans.
WestpacTrust sees the recent subdued performance from the retail sector continuing over the next few months.
Richard Miller, principal of McDermott Miller, said consumer confidence had fallen in almost all regions and population groups.
"Although all consumer groups remain optimistic there are signs that this may not last," he said.
Consumer confidence indices for Auckland and Wellington were down 7.5 and 15.0 index points respectively.
"Proximity to the government and disquiet about its apparent disarray on policy issues may be affecting Wellington confidence in continued economic recovery," Miller said.
